picks.rationale: PRIMA is the cleanest evidence in the file: a 2:1 randomized double-blind phase 3 (n=733) with a pre-specified PFS hit in the all-comer population, HR 0.62 (0.50-0.76, p<0.001), RoB2 low, NEJM. All-comer enrollment is the point. She qualifies without a BRCA mutation or a validated HRD score, so the rank-1 claim does not lean on a subgroup. Two honest caveats: PFS is a surrogate and OS was immature at the primary report (HR 0.70, 0.44-1.11, crossing 1), and grade 3+ thrombocytopenia (28.7%) and anemia (31%) run into her myelosuppression veto.
primary_concerns: Surrogate primary endpoint (PFS); OS immature at primary report with CI crossing 1
Grade 3+ thrombocytopenia 28.7% and anemia 31% collide with the severe-myelosuppression veto
HRD-positive subgroup HR 0.43 is larger but is a subgroup; the overall-population estimand is what applies here

picks.rationale: ATHENA-MONO replicates the all-comer PARP-maintenance signal in a separate phase 3 (n=538, 4:1): pre-specified ITT PFS HR 0.52 (0.40-0.68, p<0.0001), RoB2 low, JCO. Two independent registered trials hitting the same endpoint is what actually moves me on this class for a BRCA-WT tumor, and the benefit holds in the ITT and HRD-negative strata rather than only a BRCA subgroup. The surrogate-endpoint and myelosuppression caveats from niraparib carry over (grade 3+ anemia 28.7%).
primary_concerns: Surrogate primary endpoint (PFS); no mature OS in the primary report
Grade 3+ anemia 28.7%, neutropenia 14.6% against the myelosuppression veto
ALT/AST elevation 10.6% (usually transient; her baseline LFTs are normal)

picks.rationale: Replicated across two phase 3 trials she matches on indication (GOG-218 HR 0.717, 0.625-0.824; ICON7 HR 0.81, 0.70-0.94), and she is already on the backbone. The hard limit is that this is PFS only. GOG-218 found no OS benefit in the overall population, and ICON7's OS gain sat in a high-risk subgroup, which is a subgroup result from an open-label trial (RoB2 some-concern). VTE and bleeding risk is the operative safety problem given her VTE history and prior IVC filter.
primary_concerns: PFS-only benefit; no OS gain in the GOG-218 overall population
ICON7 OS benefit is a high-risk subgroup finding, and ICON7 was open-label (RoB2 some-concern: outcome ascertainment)
VTE and bleeding risk against her VTE history and prior IVC filter

picks.rationale: PAOLA-1 is RoB2 low, but the headline HR 0.33 is the HRD-positive subgroup, defined by MyChoice GIS >=42 or tumor BRCA, and she has neither. Her qualitative Altera instability call does not clear that companion-diagnostic bar, so on today's data she falls into the ITT estimand (HR 0.59, 0.49-0.72) or defaults to HRD-negative. I put it below the all-comer PARPs precisely because the impressive number is subgroup-derived and contingent on a validated GIS she has not had. Bevacizumab toxicity also stacks on PARP myelosuppression.
primary_concerns: The label-relevant HR 0.33 is a subgroup estimand she does not yet qualify for; ITT HR is 0.59
Eligibility contingent on a validated GIS (MyChoice >=42) she has not had; qualitative Altera call does not meet it
Combination grade 3+ AE ~57%; hypertension 19% plus PARP anemia 17%, stacking bev VTE/bleeding risk on myelosuppression

picks.rationale: For ovarian HER2-low IHC 1+ there is no direct efficacy evidence. The ovarian datapoint (PanTumor02, ORR 45%, n=40) enrolled IHC 2+/3+, not 1+, and is single-arm on a response-rate surrogate; the tumor-agnostic approval is IHC 3+. The IHC 1+ efficacy that exists is breast (DESTINY-Breast04 PFS HR 0.51; Breast06 HR 0.62), so the case for her tumor is cross-tumor extrapolation standing in for indication data. Layer on a single-specimen HER2 call (Altera could not stain HER2) and 10-12% ILD, and this is an investigational future-relapse option, not a maintenance pick I can support now.
primary_concerns: No ovarian HER2-low IHC 1+ efficacy data; the case rests on cross-tumor extrapolation from breast plus the DXd bystander mechanism (preclinical)
Ovarian evidence (PanTumor02) is single-arm, ORR surrogate, n=40, and enrolled IHC 2+/3+ above her tier; tumor-agnostic approval is IHC 3+
HER2 1+ rests on a single surgical-path IHC (Altera could not evaluate HER2); a confirmatory re-stain is needed before acting

notes: Why some options stayed off the ranked list. Disitamab vedotin: the only HER2-low efficacy read is an ESMO 2024 abstract (ORR ~34%) in PAM-pathway-selected breast, and the MMAE payload runs 68% any-grade and 18.7% grade 3+ peripheral neuropathy plus neutropenia, hitting both her named vetoes; abstract-only and veto-incompatible keeps it off. Letrozole looks attractive as an oral low-burden option, but the supporting study is a retrospective non-randomized comparison nested in a translational paper (ROBINS-I serious), not the single-arm phase 2 the trials row implied. GEN-1/IMNN-001 is the program she is already on, but the efficacy is sponsor topline plus an abstract (PFS HR 0.79, no CI, no p-value, no peer-reviewed full text), so it is not citable at RCT grade yet. The PI3K and MAP2K4 baskets have no ovarian efficacy estimand at all. Two workup asks would change the ranking: a validated GIS (MyChoice >=42) would move PAOLA-1 up, and a confirmatory HER2 re-stain would harden the single-specimen 1+ call before anyone acts on the HER2 axis.
